title: Quantum Observation and Gravitational Information
overview: What can a quantum observation distinguish when two states have the same gravitational-source assignment?
question: Which quantum properties remain observationally distinguishable beyond the complete Einstein-source description?
foundation: The Schwarzschild series establishes quantum scalar and gravitational-source constructions. A developing, finite-bank, fixed-background mathematical instrument motivates a more detailed inquiry into observational distinctions.
limits: A finite-bank, window-associated mathematical measurement does not establish strict field-theoretic locality, a detector realization, preservation of all physical constraints or cross-geometry observation transport.
next: Quantify accessible distinctions, test matched-frame transport and gauge compatibility, and investigate conditions for measurement-conditioned Einstein–scalar sources.
